=== ERCOT Steel Mills Comments on Proposal for Publication of New Rule 16 TAC §25.194.pdf ===
                                           PROJECT NO. 58481


     RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                             §                BEFORE THE
    LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                           §        PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                        §                 OF TEXAS


      ERCOT STEEL MILLS’ COMMENTS ON PROPOSED RULE 16 TAC §25.194,
               LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS

        The ERCOT Steel Mills1 offer the following comments on proposed rule 16 Texas
Administrative Code (TAC) §25.194 (Proposed Rule) issued by the Public Utility Commission of
Texas (Commission), relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards.

                                             INTRODUCTION

        The ERCOT Steel Mills appreciate the Commission’s efforts to implement Senate Bill 6
(SB6)2 and specifically Section 37.0561 of the Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) with the goal
of establishing clear, reasonable, and transparent standards for interconnecting new large loads in
ERCOT's power region. The ERCOT Steel Mills previously submitted comments on the Staff's
Discussion Draft and appreciate that the Proposed Rule reflects some of the recommendations
offered by the ERCOT Steel Mills and others on the earlier drafts.
        PURA §37.0561 was enacted to address concerns associated with interconnecting
significant new loads to the ERCOT grid, particularly high-demand loads that could “significantly
impact transmission needs.”3 The ERCOT Steel Mills support the proposed 75 MW threshold for
such loads and believe that the threshold should apply equally to new and expanding existing
customers (new interconnections and expanded interconnections). We offer comments and
suggested edits to the draft rule below to highlight and address how potential misinterpretation of
the applicability of the draft rule could unnecessarily affect investment decisions, financial



1
  The ERCOT Steel Mills include CMC Steel Texas, Gerdau Long Steel North America, Nucor Steel-Texas, a division
of Nucor Corporation, and Steel Dynamics, Inc.
2
  Senate Bill 6 (89th R.S., 2025) (Sen. Phil King), available at
https://capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/89R/billtext/pdf/SB00006F.pdf#navpanes=0.
3
  PURA §37.0561(c) sets the demand threshold at “75 megawatts unless the commission determines that a lower
threshold is necessary to accomplish the purposes described by Subsection (b).” Those purposes are to “support
business development in this state while minimizing the potential for stranded infrastructure costs and maintaining
system reliability.” PURA §37.0561(b).


                                                                                                                 1
 exposure, and operational certainty for existing customers, even where proposed load additions
are modest and do not “significantly impact transmission needs.”
          These standards will potentially be applied to new and existing loads, including traditional
industrial and manufacturing customers. The ERCOT Steel Mills submit these focused comments
and recommended edits to provide more clarity in proposed Section 25.194(b), the Applicability
provision, and Section 25.194(c)(9), the corresponding definition of large load customer.
Specifically, we recommend ensuring that the same applicability threshold applies to both new and
existing interconnections, namely an addition of 75 MW or more of new load, consistent with the
mandate of PURA § 37.0561. This is an important issue because an overly broad application of
the Large Load Interconnection Standards to existing customers may hinder investments that are
critical to manufacturing competitiveness, job creation, and economic retention and development.
          Our proposed edits are narrowly tailored and do not alter the fundamental structure or
policy objectives of the Proposed Rule. Rather, these edits simply clarify the Proposed Rule to
avoid unintended consequences for existing industrial facilities seeking to make investments and
process upgrades that do not materially impact the transmission grid and do not carry a significant
risk of stranded costs if the load does not materialize.

         COMMENTS ON AND SUGGESTED EDITS TO PROPOSED 16 TAC §25.194

A.        Proposed 16 TAC §25.194(b), Applicability

          The ERCOT Steel Mills acknowledge that the Proposed Rule includes meaningful
refinements to the applicability framework. Proposed Section 25.194(b) now applies to a large
load customer that seeks: (b)(1) “a new interconnection that is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts
(MW),” (b)(2) “an expanded interconnection that equals or exceeds 75 MW for the first time,” and
(b)(3) “an expanded interconnection that exceeds 75 MW by 75 MW or more.”4 While this
structure represents an improvement over the Discussion Draft, the ERCOT Steel Mills
recommend a further clarification that the Large Load Interconnection Standards apply only when
adding an additional 75 MW or more, whether it be at an entirely new interconnection or expansion
of an existing interconnection.




4
    Proposed 16 Tex. Admin. Code §25.194(b).


                                                                                                    2
          Specifically, proposed Section 25.194(b)(3) provides that the section applies to “an
expanded interconnection that exceeds 75 MW by 75 MW or more.” While this subsection appears
designed to capture substantial expansions greater than 75 MW of new load at existing sites already
above 75 MW, the phrase “exceeds 75 MW by 75 MW or more” could potentially cause confusion
or be misinterpreted to read as applying to any expansion, no matter how small, when total site
demand exceeds 150 MW. Under this unreasonable reading, a nominal existing 145 MW facility
adding 5 MW would be swept in simply because total demand crosses the 150 MW mark,
regardless of the size of the incremental expansion.
         A potential misinterpretation of this rule would subject existing industrial customers,
undergoing modest expansions (less than 75 MW), to comply with the full suite of large load
interconnection standards, such as financial security, study fees, contributions in aid of
construction, and extensive disclosure obligations. Such an outcome is inconsistent with the
statute’s intent, which targets new or expanded interconnections that exceed a Commission-
defined demand threshold, based on loads that “significantly impact transmission needs in the
ERCOT power region.”5 A modest (even a single 1 MW) increase at an existing site, especially for
a customer that has been operating in ERCOT for years, does not meaningfully impact
transmission any more than it does for a new site. Applying the Large Load Interconnection
Standards in this context would therefore be disproportionate and counterproductive, discouraging
routine investments at existing facilities and operational upgrades essential for manufacturing
competitiveness, job growth, and economic development, even where no material risk to
transmission planning or system reliability exists.
         Similarly, proposed Section 25.194(b)(2) applies the Large Load Interconnection
Standards to “an expanded interconnection that equals or exceeds 75 MW for the first time.” The
ERCOT Steel Mills propose that, for existing customers below 75 MW, the standards should apply
only when the customer adds at least 75 MW of new load through an expansion. We support
applying the 75 MW threshold to expansions in a fair and consistent manner for all existing
customers. To make that clear, the rule should be revised to provide that an existing customer
becomes subject to these additional requirements only when its incremental added load reaches or



5
 PURA §37.0561(c) (“The standards must apply only to customers requesting a new or expanded interconnection
where the total load at a single site would exceed a demand threshold established by the commission based on the size
of loads that significantly impact transmission needs in the ERCOT power region”).


                                                                                                                   3
 exceeds 75 MW for the first time. Under that approach, a 70 MW customer adding 5 MW would
not be subject to the standards, whereas a 20 MW customer adding a total of 80 MW would be.
This interpretation is consistent with PURA §37.0561 and with the rule’s apparent intent to impose
a 75 MW minimum applicability threshold on all new load, whether it is connected through a new
interconnection or through the expansion of an existing interconnection.
           As currently written, the Proposed Rule risks treating new and existing facilities
inconsistently and unfairly. A new load must meet the 75 MW threshold to qualify as a large load
customer, while an expansion of an existing facility could be subject to that designation based on
a lower incremental threshold. For example, a 5 MW new customer load would not be considered
a large load customer, but adding 5 MW to a 70 MW site or to a site that exceeds 150 MW already
could be considered a large load customer. The Commission should seek to apply the rules even
handedly to new and existing businesses alike.
           To address this potential ambiguity and inconsistent treatment of new and existing facilities
consistent with SB6, the ERCOT Steel Mills recommend the following modifications
(underline and strike-through) to the language for proposed Section 25.194(b):

           (b)     Applicability -- This section applies only to a large load customer that
                   seeks:
                   (1)   a new interconnection that is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts (MW);
                   (2)   an expanded interconnection that equals or exceeds an additional 75
                         MW for the first time; and or
                   (3)   an expanded interconnection that exceeds an existing interconnection
                         of 75 MW or more by an additional 75 MW or more.

B.         Proposed 16 TAC §25.194(c), Definitions

           The definition of “large load customer” in proposed Section 25.194(c)(9) refers to the
customer's “total expected non-coincident peak demand.”6 While this language represents an
improvement over the Discussion Draft, the ERCOT Steel Mills recommend a simple edit to add
the word “additional” to provide clarification that the rule is triggered by the additional demand
associated with a new or expanded interconnection request. This change would be consistent with
the changes recommended to Section 25.194(b) above.



6
    Proposed 16 Tex. Admin. Code §25.194(c)(9).


                                                                                                      4
        Accordingly, the ERCOT Steel Mills recommend the following conforming
modification (underline) to the definition of “large load customer” in proposed
Section 25.194(c)(9):

       (9)     Large load customer -- An entity requesting a new or expanded
               interconnection where the customer’s total expected additional non-
               coincident peak demand at a single site is equal to or exceeds 75 MW.

                                          CONCLUSION

       The ERCOT Steel Mills respectfully urge the Commission to adopt the targeted
clarifications to proposed Section 25.194(b) recommended herein, along with the conforming edit
to the definition of “large load customer” in proposed Section 25.194(c)(9). Together, these edits
would provide additional clarity in the Applicability provision and ensure the rule is implemented
consistently with the Legislature's focus in SB6 on managing significant new loads that impact
transmission needs. These clarifications would also avoid misinterpretations that lead to
unintended consequences for existing industrial facilities pursuing routine investments and
operational upgrades essential for manufacturing competitiveness that do not materially affect the
transmission grid or create a significant risk of stranded costs.
       The ERCOT Steel Mills appreciate the opportunity to provide these comments and look
forward to continued collaboration with the Commission and stakeholders.

                                               Respectfully submitted,

                                                    Harper Advisory LLC
                                                    9002 Six Pines Drive
                                                    Shenandoah, TX 77380

                                                    Sam Harper
                                                    Consultant to the ERCOT Steel Mills

                                      PROJECT NO. 58481

    LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                    §     PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                 §              OF TEXAS

     ERCOT STEEL MILLS’ COMMENTS ON PROPOSED RULE 16 TAC §25.194,
              LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS

                                   EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The ERCOT Steel Mills support the Commission’s efforts to implement Senate Bill 6 and PURA
§37.0561 through clear, reasonable, and transparent Large Load Interconnection Standards.
Our comments focus on clarifying when the Large Load Interconnection Standards apply to
expansions to existing customer load. As currently drafted, proposed Section 25.194(b) could
apply the standards to relatively small expansions at existing industrial facilities, even where the
incremental new load is modest and does not materially affect transmission planning or reliability.
The ERCOT Steel Mills support the proposed 75 MW threshold. That threshold should be applied
consistently to all new load, whether through a new interconnection or an expansion of an existing
interconnection.
•   Proposed Modifications to the Applicability Provision (Section 25.194(b)): The ERCOT
    Steel Mills recommend targeted edits to proposed Section 25.194(b) to clarify that the rule's
    applicability triggers are based on the magnitude of additional demand associated with an
    expanded interconnection request.
        (b)     Applicability -- This section applies only to a large load customer that
                seeks:
                (1)     a new interconnection that is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts
                        (MW);
                (2)     an expanded interconnection that equals or exceeds an additional 75
                        MW for the first time; and or
                (3)     an expanded interconnection that exceeds an existing
                        interconnection of 75 MW or more by an additional 75 MW or more.
•   Conforming Edit to the Large Load Customer Definition (Section 25.194(c)(9)): The
    ERCOT Steel Mills recommend adding the word “additional” to the definition of “large load
    customer” to ensure that the rule's obligations attach to the incremental demand being
    requested, not legacy load already interconnected and supported by the grid.
       (9)     Large load customer -- An entity requesting a new or expanded interconnection
               where the customer’s total expected additional non-coincident peak demand at a
               single site is equal to or exceeds 75 MW.
These clarifications would ensure that the 75 MW threshold applies to new interconnections and
existing interconnections equally and would reduce the risk of unintended policy outcomes for
existing industrial facilities pursuing incremental load additions, where customers may otherwise
delay or forgo routine investments and operational upgrades, even when such projects do not
materially affect transmission planning, reliability, or stranded-cost risk.
